by_cases hρ : ρ ∈ zerosetKfR (3/4:ℝ) (by norm_num) f
    · obtain ⟨g,hg⟩ := lem_analytic_zero_factor (7/8:ℝ) (3/4:ℝ)
        (by norm_num) (by norm_num) (by norm_num) f ha (hf0 ▸ one_ne_zero) ρ hρ
      exact ⟨g,fun _ => hg⟩
    · exact ⟨fun _ => 1,fun h => (hρ h).elim⟩
  choose g hg using hex
findings.problem: The statement of `hex` is shaped as `∀ ρ, ∃ g, ρ ∈ S → …` instead of the natural `∀ ρ ∈ S, ∃ g, …`. This is done only so that plain `choose` returns a function `g : ℂ → ℂ → ℂ` that does not depend on the membership proof. The cost is a `by_cases`, a dummy witness `fun _ => 1` for points outside the zero set, and an `.elim` branch. None of this is part of the mathematics; it is bookkeeping for `choose`. Mathlib's `choose!` exists to remove dependencies on propositional arguments like this one.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace lines 30–40 with:
```lean
  have hex : ∀ ρ ∈ zerosetKfR (3/4:ℝ) (by norm_num) f, ∃ g : ℂ → ℂ,
      AnalyticAt ℂ g ρ ∧ g ρ ≠ 0 ∧
        ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 ρ, f z=(z-ρ)^(analyticOrderAt f ρ).toNat*g z :=
    fun ρ hρ => lem_analytic_zero_factor (7/8:ℝ) (3/4:ℝ)
      (by norm_num) (by norm_num) (by norm_num) f ha (hf0 ▸ one_ne_zero) ρ hρ
  choose! g hg using hex
```
This should give `g : ℂ → ℂ → ℂ` and `hg : ∀ ρ ∈ zerosetKfR …, …`, which is the shape `final_ineq1`'s `h_σ_spec` expects. Not compiled.
findings.benefit: With this change, `hex` states exactly what `lem_analytic_zero_factor` gives: each zero in the closed 3/4-disc has a local factorisation. It is proved by a direct application of that lemma. The reader no longer has to work out why there is a case split, or why a constant-1 function appears off the zero set. The key idea, "choose a factorisation at each zero", becomes the only thing on the page. `choose!` is a standard Mathlib tactic with documented behaviour, not opaque automation.
